symptom: PC has an IP address but cannot reach the default gateway
expected_fault: Incorrect default gateway

symptom: PCs in VLAN 20 cannot communicate with other PCs in the same VLAN
topology: PC-01 → SW1 Fa0/1; PC-02 → SW1 Fa0/2
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 20 exists; Fa0/1 assigned VLAN 10; Fa0/2 assigned VLAN 20
expected_fault: PC-01 switch port assigned to wrong VLAN

symptom: VLAN 30 devices cannot reach the router
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 30 exists; show interfaces trunk: VLAN 30 not listed as allowed on trunk Fa0/24
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is not allowed on the trunk

symptom: A newly connected PC cannot communicate with devices in its department
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 40 does not exist; Fa0/5 is configured for VLAN 40
expected_fault: Required VLAN 40 is missing from the switch

symptom: Users in VLAN 10 cannot access users in VLAN 20
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: trunk is up; show ip interface brief: router subinterface G0/0.20 is down
expected_fault: VLAN 20 router subinterface is down

symptom: PC receives an IP address but cannot reach the server
expected_fault: Router has no route to the server network

symptom: PC receives an address from DHCP but cannot communicate outside its subnet
expected_fault: DHCP pool provides an incorrect default gateway

symptom: PC cannot obtain an IP address automatically
show_outputs: PC-01: IP 0.0.0.0; show ip dhcp pool: no configured DHCP pool for 192.168.10.0/24
expected_fault: DHCP pool is missing

symptom: PCs can communicate by IP address but cannot access the server using its hostname
show_outputs: PC DNS server configured as 192.168.10.50; show ip interface brief: DNS server interface is down
expected_fault: DNS server is unreachable

symptom: Remote LAN cannot communicate with the local LAN
show_outputs: R1#show ip route: route to 192.168.20.0/24 is missing; R2 route to LAN-A exists
expected_fault: Missing route on R1 to remote LAN

symptom: PC receives an IP address from the wrong network
show_outputs: PC-02: IP 192.168.30.25/24; show ip dhcp binding: 192.168.30.25; PC is connected to VLAN 20
expected_fault: DHCP pool assigns an address from the wrong network

symptom: Users can reach websites by IP address but DNS names do not resolve
topology: PC → SW1 → DNS Server → Internet Server
show_outputs: PC DNS: 192.168.10.53; nslookup example.local: Server failure; show running-config: DNS service not configured on server
expected_fault: DNS service is not configured correctly

symptom: PC can reach the DNS server but hostname resolution returns the wrong server address
show_outputs: nslookup app.local returns 192.168.20.50; expected application server is 192.168.20.60; DNS record contains incorrect address
expected_fault: Incorrect DNS record

symptom: PC cannot access a remote network although the local gateway responds
topology: PC → SW1 → R1 → R2 → Remote LAN
show_outputs: PC can ping 192.168.10.1; R1#show ip route: no route for 192.168.30.0/24; R2 has route to 192.168.30.0/24
expected_fault: Missing route to remote network

symptom: Traffic reaches the router but does not reach the remote network
show_outputs: R1#show ip route: S 192.168.30.0/24 via 192.168.20.2; R2 interface toward R1 is 192.168.20.2; route points to incorrect next hop
expected_fault: Incorrect next-hop address in static route

symptom: Users cannot access the internet after a router configuration change
show_outputs: R1#show ip route: no 0.0.0.0/0 route present; LAN interface is up/up
expected_fault: Default route is missing

symptom: PCs in VLAN 10 can communicate internally but cannot reach VLAN 20
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: Fa0/24 is trunking; show ip interface brief: G0/0.10 up/up, G0/0.20 administratively down
expected_fault: VLAN 20 router subinterface is administratively down

symptom: Users can reach the router but cannot access the application server
show_outputs: show ip route: destination 192.168.20.0/24 is present; show access-lists: deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255
expected_fault: ACL blocks client traffic to the server network

symptom: Only HTTP traffic to the server is blocked while other traffic works
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny tcp any host 192.168.20.10 eq 80; ping to 192.168.20.10 succeeds
expected_fault: ACL explicitly blocks HTTP traffic

symptom: Users from the guest network can access an internal server
show_outputs: show access-lists: no deny rule for guest network 192.168.50.0/24 to internal network 192.168.10.0/24; guest client can ping internal server
expected_fault: Guest isolation ACL is missing or incorrectly configured

symptom: Users can access the internal network but internet access fails
show_outputs: R1#show ip nat translations: no translations appear; show running-config: inside LAN 192.168.10.0/24 is not included in NAT configuration
expected_fault: LAN network is missing from NAT configuration

symptom: Internet access fails even though NAT is configured
show_outputs: show ip nat inside: G0/0; show ip nat outside: G0/1; actual LAN interface is G0/0 and WAN interface is G0/2
expected_fault: NAT inside/outside interfaces are configured on the wrong interfaces

symptom: Some internal users cannot access the internet while others can
show_outputs: show access-lists: ACL permits 192.168.10.0/24 but denies 192.168.20.0/24; NAT configuration includes both networks
expected_fault: ACL blocks internet-bound traffic from the second LAN

symptom: Wireless clients cannot see the configured wireless network
show_outputs: AP configuration: SSID is configured as CampusWiFi; client is searching for Campus_WiFi; no matching SSID is visible
expected_fault: Client is configured to use an incorrect SSID

symptom: Wireless client connects to the access point but cannot obtain an IP address
show_outputs: Client association: connected; client IP: 0.0.0.0; show ip dhcp pool: wireless VLAN pool missing
expected_fault: DHCP service is missing for the wireless network

symptom: Guest wireless users can access internal company resources
topology: Guest Laptop → AP → Guest VLAN → Router → Internal LAN
show_outputs: Guest client IP: 192.168.50.20; show access-lists: no deny rule between 192.168.50.0/24 and 192.168.10.0/24
expected_fault: Guest network isolation is not enforced

symptom: PC suddenly loses connectivity to all network resources
show_outputs: show interfaces Fa0/10: administratively down; show ip interface brief: interface is down/down
expected_fault: Switch interface is administratively disabled

symptom: PC is connected to the switch but cannot communicate with any other device
show_outputs: show interfaces Fa0/11: down/down; cable/link status indicates no active connection
expected_fault: Physical link or cable connection is down

symptom: Users lose connectivity intermittently after a switch configuration change
show_outputs: show interfaces Fa0/24: line protocol down; show interfaces status: trunk port not connected
expected_fault: Trunk interface is down

symptom: Devices in VLAN 50 cannot communicate with each other
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 50 exists; Fa0/1 assigned VLAN 40; Fa0/2 assigned VLAN 50
expected_fault: One access port is assigned to the wrong VLAN

symptom: Inter-VLAN routing works for VLAN 10 but not VLAN 30
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: VLAN 10 allowed; VLAN 30 not allowed; router subinterfaces are configured
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is missing from the trunk allowed list

symptom: A PC has an IP address but reports that the address is already in use
show_outputs: PC-01 IP: 192.168.10.25; PC-02 IP: 192.168.10.25; both devices are configured with the same address
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address detected

symptom: PC can communicate locally but cannot reach devices on another subnet
show_outputs: PC: 192.168.10.15/25; router LAN: 192.168.10.1/24; host is configured with an incompatible subnet mask
expected_fault: Incorrect subnet mask on the PC

symptom: Router interface is configured with an IP address but connected devices cannot reach it
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.10.1 administratively down; show running-config: interface is shutdown
expected_fault: Router interface is administratively shut down

symptom: Users can reach the gateway but cannot access a specific remote subnet
show_outputs: R1#show ip route: 192.168.40.0/24 is present via 192.168.20.2; R2#show ip route: no route back to 192.168.10.0/24
expected_fault: Missing return route on remote router

symptom: PC cannot ping the default gateway
expected_fault: Incorrect default gateway

symptom: Internal hosts can reach the router but cannot access the internet
show_outputs: R1#show ip route: default route present; R1#show ip nat translations: no translations; R1#show run | include ip nat: no NAT overload rule
expected_fault: Missing NAT overload configuration

symptom: PC in LAN-A cannot reach a remote network behind R2
show_outputs: R1#show ip route: no route for 192.168.40.0/24; R2#show ip route: 192.168.40.0/24 is directly connected; R1 interface toward R2 is up/up
expected_fault: Missing route to remote network on R1

symptom: PCs in VLAN 30 are not receiving IP addresses from the central DHCP server
show_outputs: PC-01: IP 169.254.10.20; R1#show ip interface brief: G0/0.30 up/up; R1#show run interface G0/0.30: interface is up; no ip helper-address shown
expected_fault: Missing DHCP relay configuration

symptom: A PC connected to the access switch cannot communicate after another device was connected to the same port
show_outputs: SW1#show interfaces status: Fa0/10 err-disabled; SW1#show port-security interface Fa0/10: Security Violation Count: 1; Maximum MAC Addresses: 1; SW1#show port-security address: Secure MAC address learned on Fa0/10
expected_fault: Port-security violation caused the switch port to enter err-disabled state

symptom: PC cannot reach the server on the remote network
show_outputs: PC0: IP 192.168.10.20, Mask 255.255.255.0, Gateway 192.168.10.1; R1 G0/0: 192.168.10.1 up/up; R1 G0/1: 192.168.20.1 administratively down/down; Server0: IP 192.168.20.10, Mask 255.255.255.0, Gateway 192.168.20.1; PC0 ping 192.168.20.10: Destination host unreachable
expected_fault: R1 GigabitEthernet0/1 is administratively shut down
